subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
passage: After lunch break in the Class 6 corridor, the vase lay in pieces and Mrs. Iyer was asking who did it. Nitin saw Hafsa look at the floor. "It was Nitin," said someone, and Hafsa said nothing. Nitin took the blame, and his eyes stung. That evening, in the school van, he said, "Hafsa, I saw you knock it." She flushed and whispered, "I was scared of my father." Nitin looked out of the window for a while. "I was hurt," he said. "I want to hear more, but I do not know yet if we are friends the same way."

qa.q: What lay in pieces in the corridor?
Why did Nitin's eyes sting when he took the blame?
qa.a: He felt betrayed, because he had seen Hafsa knock the vase and she let him carry the blame.

qa.q: What did Nitin do that avoided revenge and left room for repair?
qa.a: He told Hafsa what he had seen, listened to her reason and said he needed time to decide about the friendship.

qa.q: How might Hafsa have felt in the van when Nitin spoke?
qa.a: Hafsa probably felt ashamed and afraid, and she may have wanted to explain why she stayed silent.

grounding: A child takes blame that a friend let fall on him; he tells her what he saw, hears her out and decides slowly about repairing trust.
